resolution: Diagnosed the invisible-bookshelf report by measurement, not theory: replicated the placed-prop path headlessly and checked every durable channel — per-component winding (propagation + centroid-centered volume), painted.blob↔base.blob row alignment, full UV-footprint coverage against atlas alpha, glass run — for BOTH current and HEAD revisions, base and skin placements. All clean: the on-screen artifact came from live-session pairing (placed instances bind export-time cached geometry to the paint of the moment; the model was re-saved at 18:27 with a 144→128 topology change after the screenshots), so it should stop reproducing after reload/re-place. The investigation surfaced two REAL import-boundary traps, both now closed in Zig (rebuild required): (1) imported textures adopt OPAQUE — the world renders atlas alpha through the transparent pass while the editor preview ignores it, and this texture is 38% transparent padding, so any UV drift = invisible faces in the world only; authored glass still re-applies from the doc run, legacy packages heal on open+save; (2) imported meshes adopt consistent winding via mesh_edit.inconsistentWindingMask + normalizeSoupWinding at all four import doors, warning loudly on repair. 6 new unit tests, 42 pass, ast-check clean; doc + index hazard updated.
